transitions.overview:
Covers three scenario types where Scrum is not yet running, has lapsed, or the board no longer reflects reality. These are not ceremonies - they are structured onboarding and recovery workflows that precede ceremonies.
All three follow the same pattern: Detect scenario → sequential elicitation (lumped Q&A with conditional branching) → board audit → story review → update config.yml → establish baseline → plan first/next sprint
The ceremony playbook in `1_workflow.xml` takes over once a sprint is established. The story_review_protocol below applies within all three playbooks whenever individual items are being assessed.

story_review_protocol.description: For each item under review: run the three checks in sequence. Offer reclassification or breakdown when signals are present - do not force. Always confirm with the human before writing changes. Apply `scrum_update_story` after each item is fully settled before moving to the next.

check.name: sufficiency
check.question: Is this item understood well enough to estimate and commit to?

signals.signal: Body is vague: "research X", "figure out Y", "look into Z", "investigate..."
Team cannot agree on an estimate because the approach is unknown
An untested assumption is embedded in the scope
The item depends on an answer that hasn't been found yet

check.if_insufficient: Offer: "This looks like it needs investigation before we can commit to it. Should we convert it to a time-boxed Spike? A Spike produces knowledge, not an increment. Output would be: 'By end of sprint, we will know [specific question].' It gets a time-box (e.g. 3 days), not a story-point estimate." If confirmed: rewrite the item body with a clear research question, expected output, and time-box. Set type label to Spike.

check.name: size
check.question: Can this item realistically be completed within one sprint?

signals.signal: Item contains multiple independent deliverables that could ship separately
Item spans multiple user types, workflow steps, or data variations
Team cannot agree on scope without making large assumptions

check.if_too_large: Offer two paths: 1. "Break it into smaller stories now." - run story splitting inline. Offer splitting patterns: workflow step / user type / data variation / happy path first. Reference `references/advanced-practices.md §Story splitting` for technique details. Create child stories; keep the parent as an Epic label with a goal statement. 2. "Keep it as an Epic placeholder; refine only the first child story now." - tag the current item as Epic; create one sprint-ready child story from the most valuable slice. Defer remaining breakdown to backlog refinement. Ask: "Which path fits better for right now?"

check.name: type
check.question: What kind of work is this?

types.type: New capability that users would notice. Full DoR applies: user story format, AC defined, estimated, dependencies clear.
Unintended behaviour breaking existing functionality. DoR: repro steps, severity, affected area. AC = "repro no longer occurs." Estimates optional for small bugs; required if >2 SP.
Internal improvement with no direct user-visible change. DoR: rationale, DoD impact if deferred, estimate. No user story format required; outcome statement suffices.
Time-boxed investigation. Output is knowledge, not an increment. DoR: clear research question, expected output, time-box. No SP estimate.
Container for a set of related stories too large for one sprint. No estimate; no user story format at Epic level. Must have a goal statement. Breakdown into child stories happens in refinement.

check.if_ambiguous: Ask: "Would a user notice this change, or is it purely internal work?" User-visible → Feature or Bug. Internal → Tech Debt or Spike. If the item is clearly a cluster of features → Epic.
check.action: Update item type label via `scrum_update_story` once confirmed. Adjust DoR expectations per type before marking an item sprint-ready.

story_review_protocol.validation_close: After all three checks: "Does this item's scope feel right to you? Is there anything that should be split off, or anything missing that belongs here?" Apply `scrum_update_story` to record all agreed changes, then move to the next item.

phase.name: project_context
phase.lump: Ask together - short answers, orient the session. No tool calls yet.

questions.q: What is this project, and what is it ultimately trying to achieve?
Who is on the team, and what is each person's role?
Are there any hard external constraints - deadlines, milestones, or stakeholder commitments?

actions.action: Write `project.name` and `project.team` entries to `.github/scrum/config.yml` from answers.
Note milestone dates for use in sprint planning later.

phase.name: board_audit
phase.lump: Agent-driven. Call tools first, present findings, then ask one focused question.

actions.action: Call `scrum_orient` and read `.github/scrum/config.yml` to assess configuration completeness.
Call `scrum_get_backlog` to load all existing items.
Present inventory: "I found [N] items. [X] appear in-progress, [Y] in a backlog state, [Z] have no status. Here's the breakdown: [list titles and current status]."

phase.question: "Do any of these items reflect work that's already done, or work that's no longer relevant?"

branches.branch: Mark as Done via `scrum_set_field` with `field: 'status'` and `value: 'Done'`. Note for velocity reconstruction in Phase 3.
Label as icebox or archive. Never delete - preserve history.
Skip Phase 3. Jump directly to Phase 4. Ask: "Would you like to start by adding the first few stories together, or do you have a list somewhere we can work from?"

phase.name: velocity_baseline
phase.lump: Informal history - rough estimates are fine, exact numbers are not expected.

questions.q: Roughly how much has the team shipped in the past 4–8 weeks?
In a typical week or two, how many items or features get finished?
Was the team fully focused on this, or splitting time across other work?

actions.action: Derive a rough velocity estimate. Express in items/sprint if no estimates exist yet; convert to story points after first estimation pass.
Set `scrum.sprint.velocity_window` in config.yml.
Annotate: "Bootstrap estimate - refine after 2–3 sprints."

branch.condition: team has no sense of past throughput

branches.branch: Use capacity formula as the starting baseline: Capacity = Available Days × Focus Factor × Team Size (default Focus Factor: 0.65). Translate to story points after the first sprint's estimates are set. Announce: "We'll treat Sprint 1 as a calibration sprint - the goal is a reliable velocity reading, not maximum output."

phase.name: quality_gates
phase.lump: Ask together - both are short answers that will be refined in future retros.

questions.q: "What does 'done' mean for this project today - even informally? What has to be true before you'd consider something finished?"
"What would prevent you from starting work on an item? What makes something 'not ready yet'?"

actions.action: Write `definition_of_done` to config.yml. Keep to 3–5 items; label as v1 in a comment. Prefer concrete and verifiable over aspirational. Frame: "We'll grow this in retro."
Write `definition_of_ready` to config.yml. Minimum viable: user story format, AC defined, estimated.
Call `scrum_add_vocabulary` if the board is missing status options that match config.

phase.name: sprint_parameters
phase.lump: Mechanical decisions - ask together, agent proposes defaults.

questions.q: "How long should sprints be? (2 weeks is the standard default; 1 week for faster feedback; 3 weeks if work items are naturally larger.)"
"What day of the week works best for sprint start, planning, and review?"

actions.action: Write `scrum.sprint.length_weeks` and `scrum.sprint.start_day` to config.yml.

If field mappings are missing (`field_mapping.sprint`, `field_mapping.status`): read available board fields from `scrum_orient` and propose mappings: "I see a field called '[X]' - does that map to your sprint / status / priority?" Confirm before writing to `backends.github.field_mapping`.
If `status_display` or `priority_display` are missing: propose standard mappings and confirm before writing.

phase.name: story_review
phase.description: Review all active backlog items using story_review_protocol. Work through items grouped by status: in-progress first, then backlog. Run all three checks (sufficiency, size, type) on each item.

actions.action: After review: "Here's what's sprint-ready: [list]. Here's what needs more refinement: [list]. Here's what we converted or split: [list]."
Apply DoR checks to every item marked sprint-ready. Flag and defer those that fail.

phase.name: first_sprint
phase.description: Transition into the ceremony playbook. Use sprint_planning ceremony from `1_workflow.xml` from this point forward.
phase.question: "Should we call this Sprint 0 (setup and orientation, no delivery pressure) or Sprint 1 (real commitments from the start)? Sprint 0 is useful if the team needs to establish tooling, DoD, or working agreements first. Sprint 1 is the right call if the team already has enough context to commit."

actions.action: Call `scrum_plan_sprint` with the agreed scope and a proposed Sprint Goal.
Call `scrum_get_template` for sprint_planning artifact to record the session.
If Sprint 0: set a lightweight goal - "By end of this sprint, we have a working board, agreed DoD, and a calibrated velocity estimate."

phase.name: understand_the_pause
phase.lump: Ask together - shapes the recovery path before any tool calls.

questions.q: "When did active work stop, roughly? (A sprint number or approximate date is fine.)"
"What caused the pause? Is that root cause resolved now?"
"Have any team members joined or left since the project was active?"

actions.action: Call `scrum_get_history` to find the last active sprint and its velocity.
Compute pause length: (today − last sprint end date) / sprint length = sprints elapsed.

branch.condition: pause > 2 sprint lengths AND team unchanged

branches.branch: Proceed to Phase 2. Treat historical velocity as potentially stale - confirm before using.

branch.condition: pause > 2 sprint lengths AND team has changed

branches.branch: After Phase 2: run abbreviated onboarding (Week 0 from `sm-coaching.md §Onboarding`) for new members before re-planning. Flag this for Phase 5.

branch.condition: pause <= 2 sprint lengths AND team unchanged

branches.branch: Velocity is likely still valid. Proceed with a lighter audit - skip Phase 3.

Name the unresolved cause explicitly before planning. Ask: "What would change between now and sprint start that makes this safe to restart?" Do not commit to re-planning until there is a credible answer.

phase.name: scope_validity
phase.lump: Ask together - determines which parts of the board are still relevant.

questions.q: "Has the product direction or priorities changed since the pause?"
"Are there new external constraints - deadlines, stakeholder changes, or technical shifts?"
"Broadly: is most of the backlog still valid, or does a significant portion need re-evaluation?"

actions.action: If major scope change: flag the full backlog for story_review_protocol triage in Phase 4.
If minor scope change: note affected areas; target triage there in Phase 4.
Update `project.team` in config.yml if membership changed.

phase.name: velocity_rebaseline
phase.description: Only run if pause > 2 sprint lengths OR team composition changed.
phase.question: "The last recorded velocity was [X] SP/sprint. Given the pause and any team changes, does that still feel like a reliable planning number?"

branches.branch: Retain. Adjust `scrum.sprint.velocity_window` if the pause should not be included in the window.

Use capacity formula as the new baseline: Capacity = Available Days × Focus Factor × Team Size. Announce: "We'll treat the first sprint back as a calibration sprint - commit conservatively (60–70% of estimated capacity). The goal is to prove we can deliver again, not to maximise output."

phase.name: board_audit
phase.description: Agent-driven. Present findings, then ask the human to decide on each in-progress item. Apply story_review_protocol to any item whose scope or type may have changed.

actions.action: Call `scrum_get_sprint` (last active sprint) to load in-progress items.
Call `scrum_get_backlog` for remaining items.
For each in-progress item, offer four options: "Resume as-is / Re-estimate (context changed) / Defer to backlog / Close as won't-do."
Apply story_review_protocol to any item the human is uncertain about.
For content changes (title, body, labels): call `scrum_update_story`. For status changes: call `scrum_set_field` with `field: "status"` and the confirmed status value from `vocabulary.status`.
Archive won't-do items. Never delete - preserve history.

branch.condition: restart retrospective requested OR pause had a significant cause

branches.branch: Run a brief restart retrospective before re-planning. Ask three questions: 1. "What caused the pause - and what have we learned from it?" 2. "What's different now that makes this restart viable?" 3. "What one change would prevent the same thing from happening again?" Capture one committed change. Use `scrum_get_template` for retrospective artifact.

phase.name: recovery_planning
phase.description: Transition to ceremony playbook. The first sprint back is a calibration sprint. See `sm-coaching.md §Stale recovery` for the full recovery philosophy.

actions.action: If abbreviated onboarding flagged in Phase 1: walk new members through DoR, DoD, and sprint cadence before planning. Reference `sm-coaching.md §Onboarding`.
Ask: "What is the intended restart date?"
Call `scrum_plan_sprint` with a conservative scope (60–70% of estimated velocity).
Set a calibration Sprint Goal: "Prove the team can deliver a working increment in one sprint." Output-focused, not feature-maximising.
Call `scrum_get_template` for sprint_planning artifact.

phase.name: assess_the_gap
phase.lump: Ask together - sizes the reconciliation effort before any tool calls.

questions.q: "How far behind is the board? (Weeks, months, rough feature count - any estimate is fine.)"
"Was development happening consistently during that time, or in bursts?"
"Do you have any record of what got done - commits, release notes, changelogs, or even just memory?"

actions.action: Call `scrum_get_backlog` and `scrum_get_sprint` to load current board state.
Present inventory: "The board shows [N] items, most last touched [date range]. [X] are in-progress, [Y] are in backlog, [Z] have no sprint assigned. Let's reconcile this with what actually happened."

branches.branch: Note: reduce ceremony overhead throughout this playbook. Sprint length may be shorter (1 week). DoR can be lighter. Focus is board accuracy and forward visibility, not process compliance.

branch.condition: large gap with no records at all

branches.branch: Start from what the human remembers. Reconstruction doesn't need to be exact - the goal is a board that reflects current reality, not a perfect historical record. Announce: "We're building a working board, not an audit trail. Approximate is fine - we just need to know what's done and what's next."

phase.name: reconstruct_done_work
phase.description: Work through what actually happened. Use any available evidence. The goal: board Done column reflects real completed work before forward planning begins.
phase.question: "Walk me through what you built or shipped since the board was last updated. Rough groupings are fine - we don't need exact dates."

actions.action: For each item the human describes as completed: (a) Find a matching board item → mark Done via `scrum_set_field` with `field: 'status'` and `value: 'Done'`. (b) No matching item → create a new item and immediately mark Done. This reconstructs history without inventing fictional sprints. (c) Item was partially completed → update the body to reflect current state; split remaining work into a new open item.
Apply story_review_protocol to any item where scope is unclear during reconstruction. Reconstruction is a good time to reclassify items that were never properly typed.
Do not create sprint assignments for historical work. Mark items Done directly.

phase.name: triage_remaining_items
phase.description: Board Done column now reflects reality. Review what's still open - these are the candidates for the next sprint and future backlog.

actions.action: Present all remaining open items.
Apply story_review_protocol to each (sufficiency, size, type).
After reviewing existing items: "Are there things you're planning to build that aren't on the board yet?" Add confirmed new items. Apply story_review_protocol immediately.
Result: a clean, current backlog that reflects genuine intent.

phase.name: establish_baseline
phase.description: Reconstruct a velocity estimate from the reconciled history, if possible. If not enough data: fall back to capacity formula.

actions.action: Count Done items from Phase 2. If items have estimates: sum SP and divide by elapsed sprints (approximate). If no estimates: use item count per estimated sprint length.
Ask: "Is that pace sustainable going forward, or was it an unusual push?"
Write velocity baseline to config.yml. Annotate as reconstructed.
If DoD and DoR are not yet in config: run Phase 4 of project_bootstrap playbook now.

branches.branch: Defer velocity calculation until after the first sprint. Use capacity formula for now. Run Planning Poker during the sprint planning session. Announce: "We'll set estimates collaboratively in planning and use Sprint 1 to calibrate."

phase.name: forward_planning
phase.description: Board now reflects reality. Transition to ceremony playbook. See `sm-coaching.md §Board catchup` for the reconciliation philosophy.
phase.question: "Should we set up the next sprint now, or would you prefer to refine the backlog a bit more first?"

branches.branch: Transition to sprint_planning ceremony in `1_workflow.xml`. This is effectively the first properly-tracked sprint - treat it like Sprint 1 from bootstrap.
Transition to backlog_refinement ceremony in `1_workflow.xml`. Schedule planning for the next session.

actions.action: Call `scrum_get_template` for sprint_planning artifact when planning begins.

config_write_guidance.rule: Always read `.github/scrum/config.yml` before writing. Update only keys that have been explicitly elicited. Preserve all existing content and structure.
Never overwrite `auth.*` values. These are environment variable references - leave as-is.
For `backends.*.field_mapping`: propose values based on `scrum_orient` field discovery. Confirm with the human before writing. Field names are case-sensitive.
For `backends.*.status_display` and `priority_display`: propose the full mapping and confirm before writing. These affect all board operations downstream.
Write `definition_of_ready` and `definition_of_done` as YAML lists, one criterion per line. Add a comment `# v1 - [date]` when first written.
After any write to config.yml, call `scrum_orient` again to confirm the changes are valid and no new configuration gaps were introduced.
If a field value in config.yml requires a platform-specific ID (node ID, field ID, option ID), fetch the ID via `scrum_orient` or relevant tool - never ask the human for it.
